matt (customer): Hi - starting ~10:40 PDT we saw a flurry of 504s from the hosted inference endpoint for tenant abc123. ~20% of requests were 504/502 for a few minutes. Happening across multiple regions but most pronounced in us-east-1. Example request-id: req_0a1b2c3d. Can you take a look? Repro (simple curl):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"open-xxl","input":"hello"}' -s -D -

ish: returns 504 after ~3s.

emma (support): Thanks Matt — looking now. Do you have the full request-id header and the exact timestamp for one of the failed calls? Any SDK or raw curl? Also are you using streaming or non-streaming?

matt (customer): non-streaming. One failed response at 2025-11-03T17:40:12Z, request-id: req_0a1b2c3d, tenant: abc123. Payload is small (few tokens). Not rate-limited afaik. No special headers.

alert-bot: [ALERT] hosted-east-1/request-queue-depth > 90% (10:40:05 UTC) — sustained 120s.

alex.sre: I pulled the tenant trace. We're seeing sustained backlog in the continuous-batching queue for hosted-east-1. Per-tenant queue hit the configured limit (1000) and the gateway started early-rejecting/returning 504s on the slow tail. Batchers show high wait_ms.

alex.sre: Relevant snippets from batcher logs for tenant=abc123:

```
batcher.INFO 2025-11-03T17:40:04Z tenant=abc123 queue_size=1024 queue_limit=1024 avg_wait_ms=2380 avg_batch_size=3 pending_requests=980
gateway.WARN 2025-11-03T17:40:05Z tenant=abc123 reject=QUEUE_FULL status=504 req=req_0a1b2c3d
runtime.ERROR 2025-11-03T17:40:07Z model=open-xxl kv_cache_pressure=high alloc_retry=2
```

alex.sre: CPU/GPU utilization for the pool was normal; this looks like head-of-line blocking combined with a traffic pattern where many tiny requests prevent large batches from forming and cause batcher backpressure. The continuous-batching window is holding requests waiting for additional tokens, but backlog grows faster than consumers drain.

emma (support): Is there a short-term workaround we can offer the customer (tenant abc123) before a full fix?

jia (runtime): Short-term mitigations:
- Temporarily disable continuous-batching for tenant abc123 (fastest)
- Increase per-tenant queue_limit from 1000 -> 2048 (mitigates early-rejects)
- Route this tenant to the low-latency fast-path model variant (smaller model) as a fallback

jia (runtime): I'm going to canary the disable-batching patch for that tenant now. Steps I'm running:

```
# disable continuous batching for tenant abc123
POST /admin/tenants/abc123/config {"continuous_batching": false}
# bump queue limit
POST /admin/pools/hosted-east-1/tenants/abc123/limits {"queue_limit":2048}
```

alex.sre: Also increasing the batching immediate-drain threshold so tiny-request flood doesn't wait the full batch window. Will push config tweak to canary.

emma (support): Matt — I'm going to coordinate the temporary disable now. Please let us know if you can repro after the change (I will update here when done).

alert-bot: [INFO] executing rolling-canary -> change set id cs_20251103_1725 (target: tenant abc123)

jia (runtime): Canary deployed to 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3m. Continuous-batching disabled for abc123 and queue_limit raised. Observing reduced queue_size and fewer early-rejects.

alex.sre: Post-change logs:
```
batcher.INFO 2025-11-03T17:43:12Z tenant=abc123 queue_size=230 queue_limit=2048 avg_wait_ms=120 avg_batch_size=1
gateway.INFO 2025-11-03T17:43:13Z tenant=abc123 request=req_0a1b2c3d status=200 lat_ms=150
```

matt (customer): Confirmed — I retried the earlier curl at 17:43:22Z and it returned 200 quickly. Thanks. Any idea of the long-term fix?

jia (runtime): Long-term we need a combination: smarter adaptive batching that senses tiny-request floods and routes them to the fast-path, per-tenant adaptive queue limits tied to observed traffic patterns, and improved autoscale triggers for worker count based on queue growth rate (not just CPU/GPU). We'll open a tracking ticket in eng-runtime and propose a rollout plan.

emma (support): I'll log the customer escalation and share the workaround and timeline. Matt, we'll follow up with a postmortem and timeline for the permanent changes. Sorry for the disruption. :pray:

alert-bot: [RESOLVED] hosted-east-1/request-queue-depth returned to normal (17:45:01 UTC)

alex.sre: Filed ENG-RUNTIME-4721: "Adaptive batching + per-tenant queue autoscaling to prevent queue saturation / tail timeouts" with details and logs. Assigned to jia.

jia (runtime): I'll take the ticket. Next steps: design spike for adaptive fast-path (2 weeks), implementation (4-6 weeks), canary.

matt (customer): Appreciate the fast response. Keep me posted on the ticket and any breaking changes to config.

emma (support): Will do. Closing the incident thread once we publish the postmortem.
